name: ha--room-sensor-staleness-guard
description: LivingR/BedroomB comfort-band automations now cross-check the Xiaomi room temperature sensor against the climate unit's own ac_temp sensor. A room sensor whose numeric value has not genuinely moved (>=0.1C) in the configured window (default 5h) is treated as stale and the climate's own sensor is used instead. If both sensors are healthy but disagree beyond a tunable threshold (default 1.5C), the less comfortable (worst-case) reading wins instead of blindly trusting the room sensor.

changes: setup_room_sensor_staleness_guard.js: creates 7 input_number helpers (per-sensor last_seen_value for livingr_room, bedroomb_room_primary, bedroomb_room_secondary; per-room stale_hours + ac_disagreement_threshold for livingr and bedroomb) and 3 input_datetime *_last_moved helpers, plus a new automation id=1770077000099 '[TEST] AirCon - room sensor fluctuation tracker' (entity: automation.test_aircon_room_sensor_fluctuation_tracker) that updates *_last_seen_value/*_last_moved only when a tracked sensor's numeric state changes by >=0.1C, independent of unavailable-flicker state churn

sync_climate_setup_templates.js: buildSetup() now computes *_stale (now - last_moved > stale_hours) and *_healthy (not stale) per room sensor, then source/effective picks 'conflict_worst_case' (max in summer / min in winter / room value in neutral mode) when a healthy room sensor disagrees with ac_temp by >= the room's disagreement threshold; refactored from a self-executing IIFE into exported buildSetup/replaceSetupTemplates/applyAndRearm (module.exports) gated by require.main so callers can reuse the template patch without forcing automation.turn_on. Also fixed a regression found during TF backport: bedroomb's buildSetup no longer defined generic room/battery variables after the refactor, but the deployed log-suffix message templates (main.tf bedroomb_climate_test_log_suffix, already live) still reference {{ room }}/{{ battery }} for the 'source_room'/'source_battery' log fields — added back `room = candidate` / `battery = <matching sensor's battery>` as legacy aliases at the end of the bedroomb branch so those log fields keep rendering instead of going undefined

apply_climate_setup_templates_config_only.js: new thin wrapper that calls replaceSetupTemplates for both automations and reloads config WITHOUT calling automation.turn_on, since the comfort automations are intentionally left disabled while the user runs the AC in manual mode

main.tf: backported the same staleness+conflict Jinja logic (byte-identical to buildSetup() output) into the livingr_climate_test_setup and bedroomb_climate_test_setup locals blocks so Terraform mirrors the live config per repo convention; added a new homeassistant_automation.test_aircon_room_sensor_fluctuation_tracker resource matching the live tracker automation (3 state triggers, mode=queued, choose action with 3 per-sensor branches)

import.tf: added an import block binding homeassistant_automation.test_aircon_room_sensor_fluctuation_tracker to the existing live automation id 1770077000099, so a future `terraform apply` adopts the live automation instead of creating a duplicate

checks: C1: input_number/input_datetime helper list (WS) contains all 7 input_number + 3 input_datetime staleness-guard helpers with expected defaults (stale_hours=5, ac_disagreement_threshold=1.5, last_seen_value=0.0 pre-fluctuation)
C2: automation.test_aircon_room_sensor_fluctuation_tracker exists (REST config, id=1770077000099) and state=on
C3: /api/template render of buildSetup('livingr') + debug tail returns source/effective/room_stale/room_healthy keys with sane types (no template error)
C4: /api/template render of buildSetup('bedroomb') + debug tail returns source/effective/primary_stale/secondary_stale/primary_healthy/secondary_healthy keys with sane types (no template error)

C5: after apply_climate_setup_templates_config_only.js runs, both automation.test_aircon_livingr_room_sensor_comfort_band and automation.test_aircon_bedroomb_room_sensor_comfort_band remain state=off (config patched but NOT re-armed, since user has manual override active)

C6: main.tf syntax stays valid after the backport (brace/bracket/paren counts balanced across the whole file; `terraform fmt -check` on the new locals bodies and the new automation resource produces no diff) and the new tracker automation resource has a matching import.tf block bound to live id 1770077000099 so `terraform apply` would adopt rather than duplicate it

C7 (regression, found during backport): bedroomb's {{ room }}/{{ battery }} log-suffix fields render a real value again after adding the legacy room/battery aliases to buildSetup(), instead of going undefined -- verified via /api/template rendering 'source_room={{ room }}, source_battery={{ battery }}' against the live bedroomb setup template (result: source_room=23.5, source_battery=100.0)

notes: Eval created retroactively after live implementation (helpers + tracker automation + template patch already applied before this eval file existed) at the user's explicit request to follow the eval lifecycle going forward. C1-C2 already confirmed by setup_room_sensor_staleness_guard.js's own live output during implementation; C5 already confirmed by apply_climate_setup_templates_config_only.js's own live output. Re-verified C1/C2/C5 independently via /api/states + /api/config/automation/config, and exercised C3/C4 via /api/template (not previously run): both livingr and bedroomb room sensors currently render room_stale/primary_stale/secondary_stale=True (no genuine value movement recorded yet since the fluctuation tracker was just created) and source correctly falls back to 'climate_fallback' using ac_temp, confirming the staleness guard is live and behaving as designed. While backporting to main.tf (C6), found and fixed a real live regression (C7): the bedroomb refactor had dropped the generic room/battery variables that the deployed log-suffix messages still depend on -- fixed at the generator level (sync_climate_setup_templates.js) and re-pushed live via apply_climate_setup_templates_config_only.js before backporting the corrected version into main.tf, so live and main.tf stayed in sync throughout. C5's state=off snapshot is a point-in-time fact from when this eval was validated, not a standing invariant -- see incidents for the resolution of the deferred re-enable item.
